reaction: The cutaway brings the previously built systems together.

reaction: The downward arrow makes the slip easy to follow.
reason: Changing fingertip contact appears to provide the sensory information needed to respond to the slipping glass.
expectation: The contact information should help the hand adjust its grip and steady the glass.

effect: The changing contact led to a grip adjustment that steadied the glass, completing the chapter.
reaction: The sequence of slip, skin deformation and muscle response was a satisfying connection between the systems.

mostWorthwhile.text: Steadying the slipping glass was most worthwhile because it brought touch signals and muscle action together in a recognizable task.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the skin layers involved several predictable additions in succession. The tug and nutrient descriptions gave them purpose, but the sequence felt repetitive.

surprise.text: The description of nutrients moving from vessels in the supporting layer toward living surface cells clarified how those layers are supplied.

arbitrary.text: Treating changing fingertip contact as a separate item felt somewhat artificial, though its purpose was clear from the goal and result.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it used the assembled systems in another concrete situation. The glass sequence was more engaging to me than the repeated layer-building steps.
